To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high performance of thick films organic solar cells employing nonfullerene small molecules as the acceptors is demonstrated and the active layer thickness tolerance is over 600 nm for the first time.

(1) The conventional structure PM6:F 2Cl OSCs can maintain high performance with active layer thickness as large as 600 nm; (2) The inverted structure PM6:F2Cl OSCs exhibit high performance with active layers of thicknesses up to 500 nm, which is attributed to the improved vertical phase separation in this structure; (3) A new strategy of using a thin layer of PEDOT PSS to enhance the vertical phase separation is proposed.
we have developed efficient thick film nonfullerene organic solar cells with high performance and thickness tolerance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high performance NF OSCs with thick active layer and large thickness tolerance.
the development of efficient OSCs with thick active layers.
the development of efficient thick film NF OSCs and the underlying mechanism of the performance difference between conventional and inverted devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high efficiency thick film OSCs with active layer thickness over 500 nm have been realized.
the inverted device exhibits a more uniform vertical phase separation than the conventional device, which leads to better charge transport and collection.

we have demonstrated the high performance of thick active layer NF OSCs and the inverted structure device with the film thickness of active layer of 600 nm still maintained the PCE of 10%, which is the highest performance of the NF OSCs under such a thick active layer condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vertical phase separation is an important factor for the thick film OSCs with large thickness tolerance, and the inverted device structure is more suitable for thick film OSCs based on NFAs.

, by optimizing the device structures, high performance of NF OSCs with relatively thick active layers can be achieved and the vertical phase separation in active layers is the key to the performance of thick film OSCs.
the inverted device with thick active layer is a promising candidate for the commercialization and large scale printing process of the OSCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high performance of the thick film OSCs with NFAs can be achieved by the optimized vertical phase separation in active layer.
the inverted device structure with a large active layer is a promising approach for the large area printing of high performance organic solar cells.
it is feasible to realize high efficiency NFAs based OSCs with large active layer thickness tolerance and this work provides a new direction to develop efficient thick film OSCs.
